pr_title: Serialize units ratelimits and document StartLimitIntervalSec=infinity
pr_body:
This seems to work as expected. In the issue, doubts were raised whether it works fine with daemon-reload/daemon-reexec, and it seems to work fine. (The property cannot be set via set-property, the dbus property is 'const'. We could relax this, but that'd be a separate feature.)

Closes #29574.

<!-- devel-freezer = {"comment-id":"1810771280","freezing-tag":"v255-rc2"} -->
pr_comments: An -rc1 tag has been created and a release is being prepared, so please note that PRs introducing new features and APIs will be held back until the new version has been released.

> daemon-reload/daemon-reexec, and it seems to work fine.

I meant the internal state of `start_ratelimit` doesn't seem to be serialized.
The effect is pronounced with infinite timespan
(i.e. you allow finite number of failures but it gets implicitly reset upon those reloads).
Oh, OK. Yeah, if the interval is small, this doesn't really matter. But with an infinite interval, it makes a difference. I'll try to fix this.
Updated to serialize/deserialize trigger ratelimits and auto start/stop ratelimits.
Both fails in the Arch Linux job are unrelated (though concerning, as I've seen them in multiple CI runs already).
Ah, nevermind, the fails _are_ related, I just didn't refresh the page so it looked like a man-only change.

Ah, since the rate limits now persist through daemon-reload, something like:

```diff
diff --git a/test/units/testsuite-04.SYSTEMD_JOURNAL_COMPRESS.sh b/test/units/testsuite-04.SYSTEMD_JOURNAL_COMPRESS.sh
index 8fdf1b132e..96d096d9ad 100755
--- a/test/units/testsuite-04.SYSTEMD_JOURNAL_COMPRESS.sh
+++ b/test/units/testsuite-04.SYSTEMD_JOURNAL_COMPRESS.sh
@@ -7,6 +7,9 @@ set -o pipefail
 mkdir /run/systemd/system/systemd-journald.service.d
 MACHINE_ID="$(</etc/machine-id)"
 
+# Reset the start-limit counters, as we're going to restart journald a couple of times
+systemctl reset-failed systemd-journald.service
+
 for c in NONE XZ LZ4 ZSTD; do
     cat >/run/systemd/system/systemd-journald.service.d/compress.conf <<EOF
 [Service]
@@ -35,4 +38,5 @@ done
 rm /run/systemd/system/systemd-journald.service.d/compress.conf
 systemctl daemon-reload
 systemctl restart systemd-journald.service
+systemctl reset-failed systemd-journald.service
 journalctl --rotate
```

should make the CIs happy again.

issue_context.title: StartLimitIntervalSec=infinity is undocumented, and also is not preserved across reloads
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

253

### Used distribution

Fedora 38

### Linux kernel version used

6.5.6-200.fc38.x86_64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Manual of systemd.unit(5) doesn't state that you can use `infinity` as an interval for `StartLimitIntervalSec=` option, however, it seems to work as intuition implies (allows `StartLimitBurst` value to be contained within an unlimited timeframe).

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

`infinity` works despite being undocumented

### Steps to reproduce the problem

create a systemd unit with `StartLimitBurst=5` and `StartLimitIntervalSec=infinity` options, make it so that it fails on start (like `ExecStart=/bin/false`), then start it and observe the journal. It will stop restarting after restart count reaches 5 no matter the `RestartSec=` value.

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_
comments:
I probably had a similar use case as yours and the same intuition, FYI it did not work before https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17572 and https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17582

I've been using this "feature" since my PR was accepted.
This doesn't work as you may expect -- system reboot won't preserve the rate-limiting state. Nor does `systemctl daemon-reload`, that may be called arbitrarily.
We should have some helpers to preserve rate limits state, it was added for daemon-reload rate limits, so if something is missing it shouldn't be difficult to add

review_comments:
hmm, the cherry on top would be if you'd also add this for `u->auto_start_stop_ratelimit`.

And then also for the `trigger_limit` of Path and Socket objects
